questions: How many devices did you fabricate and measure, counting both the Josephson junctions and the tunnel probes, and how many showed the global signatures and the zero-bias peaks? You name devices A, B and C and give a tunnel-junction yield below 50%, and the totals would help a reader.
Why were the other devices set aside: only for failed tunnel probes, or for other reasons too?

Which ranges of VG, Bx, field angle and temperature did you measure beyond the ones shown? For example, Fig. 4 shows cuts at Bx = 0, 1 and 2 T; what field step and how many gate points sit behind Fig. 4l and Fig. S3l?

What does the second-best device or dataset look like? Supplementary Note S1.E answers this in part with device C. Were there other devices with one working probe, like device A, and what do their spectra show?

Your text says device B has "an approximately 35% larger cross-section than the device in Fig. 1", while Table S1 gives d x W = 21 x 70 nm for A and 36 x 70 nm for B, about 70% larger (and the Methods give d ~ 20 nm). Which is right, and what effective areas do the measured Ic periods give for each device?

For device C, Supplementary Note S1.E says "All key features are reproduced" and also that "a zero-bias conductance peak was mostly absent in this device" in Figs. S2b and c, while Fig. S3 shows "a strong increase of correlated zero-bias conductance peaks". At which VG were Figs. S2b and c taken, and how do the two sets of data fit together?

The end-to-end classification in Fig. 4l and Fig. S3l uses only the signs of the third derivative at zero bias. What noise floor or threshold separates a peak from no feature, what smoothing goes into the derivative, and how do the fractions change if you vary those choices?

For the zero-field ZBPs that depend strongly on VG (Fig. 4a-b), do wider-bias gate maps show Coulomb diamonds, resonances that split and recross, or an even-odd pattern, and do you have a temperature series for any of these peaks?
